findings.reason: the author must state whether the heading-record type is public (fixing the count and the done-when to three) or private (a `_HeadingRecord`), because the section's measure pins a figure the accounting as written cannot guarantee.
findings.text: §17's interface accounting ("two public definitions are added on `reckon/_plan_html.py`, `plan_headings` ... and the machinery-element predicate") omits the heading record type: `plan_headings` "yields a named record per heading ... so callers ... bind by name and not by tuple position", and a module-level non-underscore record class is itself counted by `interface_counts.definitions` (it counts `ast.ClassDef`, not only functions), which would make §17's growth three, not two, and fail its own done-when asserting `public_definitions` "exactly two higher than at the base"

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §17 hides the whole raw-text parser behind the private `_StructuredSectionSpanParser` and exposes only three public entry points (`plan_headings`, `structured_section_spans`, the machinery-element predicate); §16 hides the section-keyed digest and the join to the review store behind the module-private `_section_digests` and one coverage predicate; §18 collapses six inline spellings of one rule into one public predicate.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan is a consolidation: §17 names `_store.py` and `mcp_views.py` as the owners of the heading walks it converges on one reader, §18 names `plan_review.RUN_COMMENT_PREFIX` as the owner of `c-run-` (deleting promotion's `_LANDING_COMMENT_PREFIX`) and `reckon/_schema.py` as the owner of the declaration map; no re-implementation of placement, path resolution, scheduler queries or a state reader is proposed.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1477, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16/§17/§18 each state why nothing public can be retired (they extend, they do not add a family), but §17's accounting claims its addition is exactly two public definitions while the heading reader it adds yields "a named record per heading".
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §17 extends the existing raw-text `_StructuredSectionSpanParser` in `reckon/_plan_html.py` (generalising it and re-homing the store's heading helpers) rather than adding a scanner, and §16 reuses `_plan_html._TAG_RE`/`count_open_decisions` and `_fingerprint_forms` rather than inventing a second tag-stripper or digest; every owner it cites resolves (the 14-line/5-file `"data-reckon"` census, the 5-line `section-landed` census, the `c-run-` prefix in `plan_review.RUN_COMMENT_PREFIX` + `promotion._LANDING_COMMENT_PREFIX` + promotion's minting site, and the six `== "implementable"` readers all reproduce with `grep` in the worktree).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the only narrow addition is `strip_tags` on `reckon/_plan_html.py` (a public exposure of the existing `_TAG_RE` across the crew package boundary, per the plan's stated house rule rather than a second expression), and the moved `landed_section_ids` is re-homed, not doubled.
